brief: Both of the diorama's lapse hours are ONE TAP away — the clock button alternates an hour past sundown and half an hour past the next sunrise (EVE_AFTER_H / DAWN_AFTER_H). The evening one lands on a town: lamps, homers, the door. The morning one lands on the sweeper, the cart and the round figure, and courtyard.html:5679 says so in its own words. So a visitor's second tap is the emptiest view the town can show them. Give the morning a population: whatever a town does at first light that is not sweeping. COUNT IT ON HEAD FIRST — I have not re-measured this premise and you should not trust it: sample presence at sunUp+0.5 across seeds and seasons, against the night, which state.watch says holds 6-9. If the morning already holds six, say so, delete the source sentence that produced the premise, and the measurement is the deliverable.
successLooksLike: Tapping the clock from the evening lands on a morning that reads as a town waking rather than an empty set — several figures, in more than one kind of errand, at sunUp+0.5 in every season. The count at that instant comes within reach of the night's 6-9.
avoid: Do not take the supply out of a laneCap share — a rare thing needs its OWN source, which is why the round and the sweeper each have one, and a share of a budget is not a rate. Do not move the lapse target itself; the fix is what is THERE at sunUp+0.5, not when the tap lands. Anything keyed on first light keys on sunUp, never on nightF's span.
